candidates.title: Transient reduced-state comparison
candidates.purpose: Determine whether TEA and TEOA produce different transient amplitudes or decay kinetics in the P01 cobalt-containing formulation, while bounding interpretation if donor substitution also changes bulk medium properties.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV007 and EV041 support that TEOA can participate in reductive quenching and alter reduced-intermediate lifetimes in photocatalytic systems. EV018 and EV005 support transient methods for donor-sensitive carrier kinetics but also show platform dependence and incomplete species assignment. GX008 supports negative controls and TAS-type characterization in photocatalytic systems. Proposed transfer: compare donor-dependent transient observables in P01 as descriptive kinetic signatures, using no-donor and no-cobalt references to limit overassignment rather than claiming a specific cobalt intermediate a priori.

comparisons.inference: Primary descriptive contrast for donor-dependent transient amplitudes or lifetimes in the full P01 formulation. A difference supports donor-associated kinetic differences under these conditions but does not by itself identify the transient species or isolate electron-delivery causality.
Tests whether TEOA produces donor-enabled transient populations above the no-donor background.
Tests whether TEA produces donor-enabled transient populations above the no-donor background.

Compares donor-dependent signals without cobalt. Similar donor trends with and without cobalt shift interpretation toward absorber or support-side carrier dynamics rather than uniquely cobalt-associated kinetics.

Secondary contrast after pilot medium adjustment. If the donor difference persists after narrowing measured bulk-medium differences, support is stronger for donor-associated kinetic effects; if it collapses, the original contrast is bounded by medium confounding.
Assesses sensitivity of the TEOA transient signature to pilot medium adjustment; a large change indicates substantial interpretive dependence on bulk-medium conditions.

procedure: Use a pilot to choose sample handling, optical density range, probe wavelengths, and pump fluence that give stable baselines and reproducible donor-enabled signals without obvious damage or nonlinear response.
Acquire transient traces for all groups under matched preparation age, suspension density, optical path, and atmosphere handling, with dark/background subtraction and repeat preparations.

Measure and record bulk covariates that donor substitution may change, such as pH or apparent basicity proxy, viscosity-related handling differences, and scattering or absorbance differences, before interpreting kinetic contrasts.

Compare amplitudes and decay parameters only in time windows with reproducible fits and acceptable signal-to-noise, using no-donor and no-cobalt references to keep assignments descriptive unless independently corroborated.

If feasible from the pilot, repeat the TEA versus TEOA comparison under medium-adjusted conditions designed only to narrow measurable bulk differences, then report whether the donor contrast persists, shrinks, or becomes ambiguous.
measurements: Transient absorption or analogous pump-probe amplitude at selected probe wavelengths
Decay kinetics or characteristic lifetimes in reproducible time windows
Dark and no-donor background traces for artifact detection
No-cobalt reference traces to separate cobalt-associated changes from absorber or support-side dynamics

Bulk covariates measured for each donor condition, including pH or comparable acidity/basicity readout, optical density or scattering proxy, and handling notes relevant to viscosity or suspension behavior
Statement of assignment confidence level, distinguishing descriptive donor-sensitive transients from specifically assigned cobalt intermediates
candidates.supports: Support for H02 would be a reproducible TEA versus TEOA difference in transient formation, amplitude, or persistence in the full P01 formulation, with donor-enabled signals above no-donor background and a contrast that is absent or smaller in no-cobalt references or that persists after medium-adjustment pilots. This supports donor-associated kinetic differences consistent with altered upstream photoredox delivery, while remaining agnostic about exact intermediate identity unless cross-checked independently.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against a strong upstream donor-kinetics account would be closely matched TEA and TEOA transient observables in cobalt-containing P01 under both baseline and medium-adjusted conditions, provided the method is sensitive enough to detect donor-enabled signals and controls behave as expected. If catalytic selectivity still differs elsewhere under such matched transient behavior, interpretation shifts toward downstream chemistry or unobserved states.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if signals are too weak, unstable, or dominated by scattering, photothermal artifacts, or degradation; if donor substitution changes bulk-medium properties so strongly that medium-adjusted comparison is not feasible; if no-cobalt references show similar donor differences that cannot be separated from cobalt effects; or if assignments remain too uncertain to connect the transient contrast to the catalytic manifold beyond a descriptive observation.
candidates.parameter_selection: Select probe wavelengths and fitting windows by pilot spectra on baseline donor-containing and no-donor samples, choosing regions with adequate signal-to-noise and minimal artifact. Set pump fluence below nonlinear or damaging regimes by fluence-dependence checks. Keep preparation age, optical density range, and path length matched across groups. If medium adjustment is attempted, choose adjustments only after measuring which bulk properties differ most between TEA and TEOA in the actual samples; do not assume a literature recipe. If adjustment introduces new instability, report only the baseline descriptive comparison.
candidates.limitations: Species assignment in a heterogeneous supported system is provisional, and transient differences do not uniquely prove electron flow into a specific cobalt intermediate. Donor substitution can co-vary pH, viscosity, ionic environment, adsorption, and suspension stability, so even a clear transient difference may reflect combined effects. No-cobalt controls help bound interpretation but do not recreate the same interfacial environment as cobalt-containing samples.

candidates.title: Matched TEA/TEOA photophysics-to-products correlation in the Co-bpy baseline, with optional homogeneous bridge
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA-versus-TEOA substitution changes donor-side quenching or transient reduced-state observables in the same direction as any CO/H2 shift under otherwise matched conditions, while explicitly limiting inference to correlation-versus-discordance rather than causation.
candidates.source_to_proposal: Sources support donor-dependent quenching measurements and show that donor identity can change irradiation-time photochemical behavior, while catalytic systems require CO and H2 to be quantified together with catalyst-free background controls. This proposal transfers those observations into a matched TEA-versus-TEOA comparison in the recommended Co-bpy platform, and optionally into a supplementary homogeneous cobalt/Ru bridge only to test directionality transfer. Any agreement would be supportive correlation, not proof that donor-side photophysics is the sole or shared cause of selectivity.

comparisons.inference: Primary single-factor test of whether donor identity shifts both donor-side observables and catalytic CO/H2 outputs under matched P01 conditions.
Checks whether donor substitution changes background photochemistry or H2 formation without cobalt, bounding catalyst-specific interpretation.
Assesses cobalt-dependent contribution under TEOA, but because cobalt omission changes the catalytic manifold this is a necessity/background contrast rather than a donor-side causal test.
Assesses cobalt-dependent contribution under TEA, again as a necessity/background contrast rather than a donor-side causal test.
Optional single-factor donor comparison in the supplementary bridge to test only whether photophysical and product directionality is transferable across platforms, not whether mechanism is shared.

procedure: Verify a chemically matched P01 baseline from the supplied recommendation, then prepare paired TEA and TEOA formulations with all non-donor components, reactor geometry, gas handling, and analytical workflow held fixed; include cobalt-omission controls and add the optional P02 bridge only after P01 matching is demonstrated.

For each group, collect donor-side photophysical data on the actual reaction mixture or the closest justified sub-mixture: steady-state emission or absorbance changes suitable for quenching analysis, and a transient optical readout assigned only as a reduced-state or charge-carrier proxy after background subtraction and reference checks.

Run matched photocatalysis on the same formulations and quantify both CO and H2 with time-resolved sampling if signal is above detection limits; analyze no-cobalt groups in parallel to estimate donor/photosensitizer/support background contributions.

Compare the direction and reproducibility of donor-dependent photophysical changes against donor-dependent CO/H2 changes across replicate runs, and treat agreement as correlation evidence and disagreement as evidence favoring downstream or parallel explanations rather than a direct causal verdict.

If the optional bridge is used, evaluate whether donor substitution gives the same qualitative direction of photophysical and catalytic change in P02, while explicitly not treating cross-platform agreement or disagreement as decisive for shared mechanism.
measurements: CO amount and H2 amount from the same gas-analysis workflow; derived selectivity reported only as a transformation of measured products, not as a sole readout.

Emission intensity or lifetime changes of the light-absorbing component versus donor identity for matched sub-mixtures; this reports quenching behavior but cannot alone identify the exact quencher or catalytic intermediate.

Transient absorbance or equivalent time-resolved optical signal assigned to a reduced-state or charge-carrier proxy using references and backgrounds; this can indicate donor-dependent formation or persistence of a transient species but cannot by itself establish the active cobalt state.
Background product formation in cobalt-omission groups to bound donor, photosensitizer, or support contributions.
If the optional bridge is used, the same classes of photophysical readouts and product measurements in P02 to test directionality transfer only.
candidates.supports: H02 is supported if, across matched TEA and TEOA runs in P01, donor substitution produces a reproducible shift in at least one donor-side quenching or transient reduced-state observable and the catalytic CO/H2 output changes in the same directional sense, while cobalt-omission controls do not fully account for the product shift. Similar directionality in the optional P02 bridge would strengthen the case that donor-side behavior is a plausible contributor, but not establish causation or a shared mechanism.
candidates.refutes: H02 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give similar donor-side quenching and transient observables within experimental resolution in P01, yet CO/H2 differs reproducibly beyond the bounded background seen in cobalt-omission controls. That outcome would favor downstream explanations such as proton-management, catalyst-state, substrate-binding, or other donor-induced changes not captured by the selected photophysical observables.
candidates.inconclusive: The result is inconclusive if P01 TEA and TEOA cannot be matched reproducibly, if photophysical signals are below assignment confidence or dominated by scattering or support artifacts, if background product formation is too large to isolate cobalt-dependent behavior, if multiple observables shift in inconsistent directions, or if the optional bridge behaves differently in ways that can equally reflect platform mismatch rather than mechanism.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent donor concentration, catalyst loading, light intensity, or sampling times. Start from the literature-anchored P01 baseline formulation and verify exact values from the supplied system recommendation. Before the full comparison, run a pilot to choose a dilution window that keeps optical signals measurable without changing component identities, confirms linear detector response, and avoids complete inner-filter saturation. Choose catalytic sampling times by first bracketing an early, mid, and later illumination interval where both CO and H2 remain above detection and the no-cobalt control stays interpretable. For the optional P02 bridge, first confirm that the TEOA formulation reproduces observable quenching before introducing TEA as the single-variable comparator.
candidates.limitations: This design tests correlation versus discordance, not causation. P01 support effects may decouple measured optical observables from the chemically active manifold. A reproducible correlation does not exclude coupled proton-transfer or cobalt-speciation changes, and a lack of correlation may reflect insensitive observables rather than true absence of donor-side differences. Cobalt-omission contrasts are inherently necessity/background tests because omitting cobalt changes the catalytic manifold and may alter charge recombination. The P02 bridge improves photophysical interpretability but is not chemically identical to the Co-bpy/g-C3N4 target, so only bounded directionality transfer is justified.

candidates.title: Donor-radical detection under TEA versus TEOA substitution
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes detectable donor-derived radical signatures under illumination in a matched cobalt comparison matrix. This probes donor-side reactive intermediates rather than catalytic products and asks whether any spectroscopic difference is reproducible and light-dependent.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV016 reports EPR spin-trapping detection of TEOA-derived radicals and notes similarity to TEA-derived adducts with TEOA line broadening attributed to viscosity; EV011 supports that both TEA and TEOA can generate alpha-aminoalkyl radical reductants after excited-state quenching; GX018 provides the transferable framework that sacrificial-donor radical cation and radical species can arise in photochemical quenching while their exact mechanistic role remains uncertain. Proposed transfer: compare TEA and TEOA within one matched cobalt-containing formulation, add fully matched dark and no-absorber controls for each donor, and keep inference limited to donor-side radical observables rather than catalytic causation.

comparisons.inference: Primary donor-substitution contrast. A reproducible difference in radical-associated signal appearance, spectral pattern, or time profile supports donor-dependent upstream photoredox differences; similar behavior weakens this explanation but does not by itself exclude it.
Tests whether the TEOA radical-associated signal is light-dependent rather than caused by handling, spontaneous donor oxidation, or probe background chemistry.
Tests whether the TEA radical-associated signal is light-dependent under the same matrix.
Bounds absorber-free background signal for TEOA. If the illuminated no-absorber control shows comparable signal, donor-radical assignment to the photoredox route is weakened.
Bounds absorber-free background signal for TEA. Parallel donor-matched background control removes the prior confounding of donor identity.

procedure: Select the cleaner matrix for radical readout, preferring the more homogeneous option if P01 scattering or support broadening prevents interpretable spectra, while keeping donor substitution otherwise matched.
Run a pilot to identify a probe level and illumination window that give a stable baseline and a resolvable light-dependent signal above dark and no-absorber controls without obvious absorber loss.
Acquire time-matched radical-detection spectra for all groups with identical preparation, irradiation history, and acquisition settings, interleaving TEA and TEOA runs to reduce drift bias.
Compare signal presence, line shape, linewidth, and growth or decay behavior across donor substitution while explicitly checking whether the same donor shows comparable signal without absorber.

If donor differences are observed, cross-check assignment conservatively against donor-matched controls and linked quenching or transient experiments rather than treating one spectral feature as mechanistic proof.
measurements: EPR or equivalent radical-detection spectra for illuminated, dark, and no-absorber donor-matched samples
Signal presence or absence relative to donor-matched dark and no-absorber backgrounds
Line shape and linewidth, noting that broader features may arise from viscosity or motion effects rather than different radical identity
Time-dependent growth and decay of radical-associated signals under matched irradiation and acquisition windows
If feasible, parallel absorber integrity check by optical spectroscopy; this does not identify the radical itself
candidates.supports: Support for H02 would be a reproducible donor-substitution effect under matched conditions in which TEA and TEOA differ in radical-associated signal behavior, both illuminated donor-containing samples exceed their donor-matched dark controls, and donor-matched no-absorber controls remain clearly smaller. Stronger support occurs if the same donor ranking also appears in linked quenching or transient-state measurements.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H02 as a dominant explanation would be closely similar TEA and TEOA radical-detection behavior across repeated matched runs, with clean light dependence and low donor-matched background, especially if linked quenching observables are also similar while catalysis still diverges. That outcome shifts attention toward downstream proton-transfer, catalyst-state, substrate-binding, or medium effects.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive outcomes include no resolved signal for either donor, strong probe or background chemistry, severe overlap or broadening preventing assignment, absorber instability during acquisition, or donor differences that are comparable to donor-matched no-absorber backgrounds. Observation of a radical-associated signal alone cannot establish that it is the productive reductant or that it controls CO versus H2.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not import donor loading, trap concentration, or irradiation time from unrelated papers as fixed values. Use a short pilot series to choose the lowest probe level giving a stable baseline and the shortest acquisition window that resolves a light-dependent signal without obvious bleaching or runaway background. After calibration, keep solvent matrix, atmosphere, irradiation geometry, and acquisition settings identical across TEA and TEOA. If P01 remains spectrally uninterpretable, move this candidate to P02 and treat transfer back to P01 as provisional.
candidates.limitations: Radical trapping can perturb chemistry, and observed adducts may be secondary trapped products rather than the immediate quenching intermediate. TEA and TEOA can differ in viscosity and line broadening, so spectral differences are not automatically identity differences. In P01, heterogeneity may obscure donor-radical detection. This experiment does not measure CO or H2 and cannot by itself establish catalytic causation or equal effective excitation.
